name: Price securities and produce the daily fund valuation (one daily valuation)
summary: Every business day the pricing team values the fund's public holdings so that Total Fund Management, Risk and liquidity forecasting can manage exposures the next morning. Vendor closing prices, evaluated bond prices, derivative prices and FX rates load overnight and automated rules flag missing, stale, zero and out-of-tolerance prices. Early the next morning analysts work the exceptions by asset class, ask dealers for quotes, challenge doubtful evaluated prices with the vendor and propose overrides, which a senior approves; halted or illiquid instruments go to Finance valuations for a fair value adjustment. The latest private and external fund values are applied, SimCorp runs the valuation, the movement is checked against benchmarks and the senior signs it off. Illiquid bonds, OTC derivatives, late vendor files and corporate action jumps make the morning slow.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund investment manager that invests one fund globally with mostly internal teams and values its public holdings daily in SimCorp Dimension from several price vendors.
baseline.notes: Private holdings change value only when the quarterly valuation is approved; the daily valuation carries them at their latest approved value rolled forward for cash flows.

trigger: North American markets close on a business day and the last regional vendor price files and FX rates become available.
end_state: The signed-off prices and net asset value by portfolio and account are published to Total Fund Management, Risk, liquidity forecasting and the month-end close.

volume.seasonality: Exception counts rise on volatile market days, around index rebalances, market holidays in one region, and month and quarter ends when prices also feed the close.

evidence.note: One valuation per Toronto business day, as in the organisation file's process map.

Title and loaded cost from the organisation file. Touch minutes on the exception steps are team person-minutes, as several analysts split equities, fixed income and derivatives in parallel; the rest of the team's day goes to challenge follow-up, month-end pricing and performance inputs.

systems.name: SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Risk analytics platform (potential loss, limits, stress tests)
Vendor end-of-day price and evaluated pricing feeds (exchange prices, evaluated bond prices, FX rates, broker quotes)

steps.name: Load vendor end-of-day prices and FX rates
steps.description: As each region closes, scheduled jobs load exchange closing prices, evaluated bond prices, derivative settlement prices and the closing FX rates from the price vendors into the SimCorp price tables, with a primary and a secondary source for most instrument types.

error.defect_description: A vendor file is late, partial or carries stale or zero prices.

evidence.note: Quoted prices and vendor or broker pricing named in the fair value policies; data feed risks from RG 94. Delivery timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run automated price validation rules
steps.description: Validation rules compare each price with the secondary source, with the previous day and with its index or curve move, and flag prices that are missing, zero, unchanged for several days or outside tolerance, producing the exception list by asset class.

error.defect_description: None introduced; poorly set tolerances let errors pass.

control.basis: Pricing and valuation policy: automated stale, missing, zero and tolerance checks against secondary sources and benchmarks

evidence.note: Monitoring of movements outside acceptable ranges and stale-price definitions per asset class.

steps.name: Check load completeness and position coverage
steps.description: At the start of the early shift an analyst confirms every vendor file arrived, then checks that every position in the reconciled position record has a price and every currency has a rate, listing new securities with no price.

error.defect_description: A missing price is overlooked and the position is valued at the old price.

next.condition: file missing or securities without a price

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file says TFM and Risk use the valuation the next morning, which implies an early-morning pricing shift.

steps.name: Request missing prices or a re-delivery
steps.description: The analyst asks the vendor's support desk to re-send or correct the file, sets up a price source for new securities with investment data management, or requests a quote from the trading desk's brokers for instruments no vendor covers.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the vendor or broker to supply the price
steps.description: The vendor re-delivers the file or the broker sends a quote; if nothing arrives before the release deadline the previous price is carried and flagged as stale.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Work equity and listed fund price exceptions
steps.description: Analysts check each flagged equity, ETF and listed fund price against the exchange close in Bloomberg, look for splits, special dividends, halts and ticker changes that explain a jump, and either accept the price or propose the secondary source or an override.

error.defect_description: A wrong price is accepted as a genuine move.

evidence.note: Stale, zero and out-of-tolerance prices and secondary-source review; minutes are the author's estimate of team effort.

steps.name: Work fixed income price exceptions
steps.description: Analysts compare flagged evaluated bond prices with the move in the benchmark curve and the issuer's spreads, the secondary vendor and any dealer runs, and decide whether the vendor price is credible or needs a challenge or override.

error.defect_description: An evaluated price that lags the market is accepted.

evidence.note: Bonds valued on benchmark curves and issuer spreads; oversight of pricing services with price challenges. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check derivative and OTC valuations
steps.description: Analysts check futures and listed option settlement prices, compare model values of swaps, forwards and OTC options with counterparty and collateral marks, and investigate large differences in curves or volatility inputs.

error.defect_description: A model input error is missed.

next.condition: prices need broker quotes or a vendor challenge

evidence.note: OTC derivatives valued with models and consensus pricing from brokers or vendors; branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request broker quotes and raise vendor challenges
steps.description: For doubtful bond or derivative prices the analyst asks two or three dealers for quotes through Bloomberg or email and logs a formal challenge with the evaluated pricing vendor, attaching the evidence. The challenge outcome is tracked over the following days.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Initiating price challenges is part of pricing service oversight; quote practice is the author's description.

steps.name: Wait for dealer quotes
steps.description: Dealers answer the quote requests during the morning; quotes that do not arrive before the cut-off leave the vendor or previous price in place with a stale flag.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare override proposals with evidence
steps.description: The analyst enters each proposed override, secondary-source switch or stale-price carry in SimCorp with a reason code, the evidence (quotes, exchange data, curve move) and the value impact.

error.defect_description: Override keyed with the wrong price or currency.

evidence.note: Overrides require a reason code and reviewer approval.

steps.name: Approve price overrides and stale exceptions
steps.description: A senior associate who did not propose them reviews the overrides, secondary-source switches and stale prices beyond the policy limit with their evidence and approves, rejects, or sends instruments that need a fair value judgment to Finance valuations.

error.defect_description: An unsupported override is approved.

control.basis: Pricing policy: price overrides need a reason code and approval by someone other than the preparer, within internal control over financial reporting

evidence.note: Override approval from FundCount; ICFR framework from the annual report.

steps.name: Approve a fair value adjustment
steps.description: A Finance valuations senior reviews halted, suspended, defaulted or thinly traded instruments, or a market closed on a holiday, and approves a fair value adjustment or model value under the valuation policy, recording it for the Valuation Committee.

error.defect_description: Adjustment judgment later proves wrong.

control.basis: Valuation policy with Finance oversight independent of investment departments and Valuation Committee governance; IFRS 13 exit price measurement

evidence.note: Finance oversight of valuation independent of investment departments and Valuation Committee governance; IFRS 13 exit price.

steps.name: Apply the latest private and external fund values
steps.description: The analyst checks that private holdings carry their latest approved quarterly valuation rolled forward for capital calls and distributions since that date, that external fund values reflect the latest administrator NAV, and that FX rates match the approved source.

error.defect_description: A cash flow since the valuation date is not rolled in.

evidence.note: Fund investments at NAV reported by managers; use of last available or preliminary values with later adjustment.

steps.name: Run the daily valuation
steps.description: SimCorp values every position with the approved prices and FX rates and produces the net asset value by portfolio, asset class and investment department, and for the base and additional plan accounts.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: SimCorp Dimension used for portfolio accounting and performance; run timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the valuation movement
steps.description: The analyst compares each portfolio's change in value with its benchmark index and currency moves, sorts positions by profit and loss, and flags moves that the market does not explain.

error.defect_description: An unexplained move is passed.

evidence.note: Tracking prices against benchmarks as a monitoring control.

steps.name: Investigate an unexplained valuation movement
steps.description: The analyst traces the move to a wrong price, a missing corporate action adjustment or a position error, asks reconciliation or trade support when the quantity is wrong, and corrects the price before re-running.

error.defect_description: Wrong correction.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign off and release the daily valuation
steps.description: The senior associate reviews the exception summary, open challenges, stale prices and the movement review and signs off, which releases the valuation to Total Fund Management, Risk and liquidity forecasting.

error.defect_description: Release with an open material exception.

control.basis: Pricing and valuation policy: daily sign-off of price validation before the valuation is released

evidence.note: Final approval separated from preparation (FundCount); daily release deadline is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Publish the valuation and prices downstream
steps.description: The signed-off prices and net asset values are published to the data platform and the risk platform, where Total Fund Management, Risk and liquidity forecasting pick them up for the morning's exposure, limit and rebalancing work.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: vendor correction or position change arrives after release

evidence.note: Downstream use from the organisation file's process map; share of late corrections is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Process a late correction and re-release
steps.description: When a vendor correction or a late position fix arrives after release, the analyst loads the corrected price or waits for the position fix, tells Total Fund Management and Risk which numbers will change, and re-runs the valuation for sign-off.

error.defect_description: Downstream users keep the earlier numbers.

evidence.note: Rectification should be documented (RG 94); share and timing are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Missing vendor file or unpriced new security
exceptions.description: A vendor file is late or partial, or a new security has no price source; the analyst requests a re-delivery or a quote and carries the old price if nothing arrives.

exceptions.name: Doubtful evaluated price challenged
exceptions.description: Dealer quotes are requested and a challenge logged with the vendor; an override is proposed and approved for the day while the challenge is followed up.

exceptions.name: Fair value adjustment by Finance valuations
exceptions.description: A halted, suspended, defaulted or thinly traded instrument, or a closed market, needs a judgment that Finance valuations approves.

exceptions.name: Unexplained valuation movement
exceptions.description: A portfolio moves more than its benchmark explains; the analyst traces and corrects the price or position and re-runs.

exceptions.name: Correction after release
exceptions.description: A vendor correction or late position fix forces a re-run after the valuation was published, and downstream users are told.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the North American market close on day T to release of the signed-off valuation
benchmarks.population: Daily valuation of public holdings at a large in-house asset owner

evidence.note: No published figure. The organisation file says TFM and Risk use the valuation the next morning; the author assumes release around 9 to 10 a.m. Toronto time, about 17 to 18 hours after the close, slipping towards noon on difficult days.

benchmarks.metric: minimum valuation frequency for total fund returns
benchmarks.population: Asset owners claiming compliance with the 2020 GIPS standards

evidence.note: GIPS 22.A.20 and 22.A.30.

pain_points.description: Evaluated bond prices and OTC derivative values lag fast markets, so analysts spend the morning gathering dealer quotes and logging challenges whose outcome arrives days later.

evidence.note: Price challenges in pricing service oversight; bonds and OTC derivatives valued from curves, spreads, models and broker consensus.

pain_points.description: Vendor feeds carry stale, zero and out-of-tolerance prices and wrong FX rates that must be caught before release.

evidence.note: RG 94 lists these data feed errors.

pain_points.description: Private holdings are carried at lagged quarterly values, so the daily valuation of a large part of the fund is an estimate.

evidence.note: Use of last available or preliminary values; private investments valued quarterly.

pain_points.description: The morning deadline is tight; late corrections after release force re-runs and messages to Total Fund Management and Risk.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

sources.title: Unit pricing: Guide to good practice (Regulatory Guide 94)
sources.supports: Commercial data feeds for listed equity and derivative prices may include stale prices, zero amounts or daily movements outside accepted tolerances, and incorrect FX rates are seen; monitoring controls should measure movements outside acceptable ranges and track prices against benchmarks; estimates must be checked against up-to-date prices and values should not be stale; rectification documented.

sources.title: NAV Oversight: Controls, Review Workflow, and Common Breakpoints
sources.supports: Stale prices defined per asset class and escalated above the policy limit; exceptions where a secondary pricing source was used are reviewed; illiquid assets need an approved methodology and memos; overrides need a reason code and reviewer approval; one FX source; stale pricing as the first common breakpoint.

sources.title: 17 CFR 270.2a-5 Fair value determination and readily available market quotations
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: US fund rule requiring assessment of valuation risks, consistent methodologies, testing of methodologies, and oversight of pricing services including initiating price challenges as appropriate; used here as a description of common practice, not a rule that binds the organisation.

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement
sources.supports: Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction (an exit price).

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Total funds valued at fair value under a written valuation policy; when the last available historical price or a preliminary estimate is used the asset owner assesses the difference and adjusts when the final value arrives; total funds valued at least monthly and private market portfolios at least quarterly.

assumptions: The pricing team works an early-morning shift so the valuation can be released before Total Fund Management and Risk start; the overnight wait before the first analyst step is set to about 11 hours.
Touch minutes on the parallel exception steps (s06 to s08) are team person-minutes; the simulator adds them in sequence, so its cycle time runs longer than the real morning.

Branch shares (12% days with missing files, 45% with challenges, 8% of override sets needing Finance valuations, 12% unexplained movements, 5% late corrections) are the author's estimates; no public source gives them.
val_senior (Finance valuations) approves fair value adjustments for public instruments; the organisation file places daily pricing in investment operations and independent valuation in Finance.
A vendor price feed system (price_feeds) is added because the organisation file lists Bloomberg but no separate evaluated pricing feed; vendor names are not public.
US Rule 2a-5 does not apply to this Canadian organisation; it is cited only as a description of common pricing service oversight practice, including price challenges.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's, which include incentive pay and a 1.25 overhead factor and sit far above the Job Bank Toronto median for NOC 11109 (34.62 an hour, 2023-2024).
The simulated median cycle time (about 1.2 days) is above the 0.75-day benchmark estimate mainly because the parallel exception steps are added in sequence by the simulator.
